THIS MFA HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT ON 09.02.2023, COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:-
 JUDGMENT
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties the same is taken up for final disposal.

2. Not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation granted by the Tribunal for the injury suffered by him in a motor vehicle accident dated 12.02.2012, petitioner has come up with this appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short) seeking enhancement.
3.
For the sake of convenience the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
4. FACTS:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 12.02.2012, he was riding Motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-04/H-9730 ('Motor Cycle' for short) from Gulbarga towards Mahagaon Village.
His friend Mustafa was the pillion rider.
When they were near Safari Dhaba, a lorry bearing registration No.MWU- 3409 ('the offending vehicle' for short) was proceeding ahead of the motor cycle.
However, the driver of the offending vehicle suddenly stopped the lorry without giving any signal.
As a result of which, the motor cycle dashed against the offending vehicle.
In the said accident, the petitioner and his friend sustained injuries.
Petitioner took treatment at Government Hospital, Gulbarga, Baseveshwar Hospital, Gulbarga, Ganga Institute of Neurosciences and Trauma Care Hospital, Solapur.
He has also taken treatment at LV Prasad Eye Institute, Hyderabad.
Despite prolonged treatment, he is not completely cured.
After the accident, he was not able to work as he use to and as such, suffering loss of income.
As the driver, owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation and prays to allow the petition.
5. Though appeared through counsel, respondent No.3 has not filed objections.
Respondent Nos.1 and 2 have filed separate objections disputing the age, occupation, income of the petitioner and that the accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: 2 specifically pleaded that the accident occurred due to the sole rash or negligent act on the part of the petitioner.
He was riding the motor cycle in a rash or negligent manner without maintaining minimum distance between the motor cycle and the offending vehicle.
Thereby, petitioner has contributed towards the cause of the accident.
Suppressing these facts, he has filed this petition.
Respondent No.2 has disputed the nature of injury suffered and that it has resulted in permanent partial disability affecting his earning capacity and income.
Petitioner was not having a valid driving licence and as such, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation and prays to dismiss the petition.
6. Based on these pleadings, Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
7. In support of his case, petitioner has examined himself as PW-1 and Eye Specialist as PW-2 and Orthopaedic Doctor as PW-3.

He has relied upon Exs.P-1 to P-13.
8.
Respondents have not led any oral or documentary evidence on their behalf.

9. Vide the impugned judgment and award dated 14.09.2016, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition granting compensation in a sum of Rs.3,84,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a. and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same.

The details of compensation granted are as under:

Total 3,83,568  Rounded off 3,84,000  10.
Respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
11. Challenging the impugned judgment and award, petitioner has filed this appeal under Section 173(1) of the Act.

Vide judgment and award dated 16.02.2018, Co-ordinate bench of this Court set aside the impugned judgment and award and remanded the case to the Tribunal with an observation that there is no evidence placed on record as to whether at the time of accident, petitioner was wearing helmet and in order to ascertain this fact and give a finding as to whether by not wearing Mohd.Jaffar S/O Saleem Miyan vs M.A.Khaleel S/O M.A. Jabbarand Ors on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38848952/

12. After the remand, petitioner has given further evidence and got marked Ex.P-14.
In the meanwhile, the petitioner approached the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No.7618/2022 (Special Leave to Appeal (C) No.18057/2018).
Vide order dated 18.10.2022, the Hon'ble Supreme Court set aside the order of remand passed by co-ordinate bench of this Court and directed this Court to decide the appeal in accordance with law.

13. Heard arguments and perused the records.
14.
In the petition, petitioner has claimed that at the time of accident, he was aged about 25 years.
However, he has not produced any evidence to prove his age.
Therefore, based on the Wound Certificate at Ex.P-4, the Tribunal is justified in taking the age of the petitioner as 28 years and as such, 17 as the appropriate multiplier.
Though the petitioner has pleaded that at the time of accident, he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month, he has not produced any evidence to prove his exact income.
Therefore, the Tribunal has taken his income on notional basis at Rs.6,000/- per month.
Since the accident is of the year 2012, based on minimum wages, the notional income of the petitioner ought to have been taken at Rs.6,500/- per month.
15. As per the evidence of PW-2, Ophthalmologist, petitioner has lost eye sight in his left eye and he has calculated the disability at 30%.

Even as per the schedule in the Workmen's Compensation Act,
1923 also, loss of eye sight in one eye, the disability is to be taken at 30%.
16. In addition to loosing the eye sight, petitioner has sustained fracture and other injuries.
PW-3 Dr. Rajendra Kothari has evaluated the Orthopaedic disability of the petitioner at 30% of the whole body.
However, he is not a treating Doctor.

Therefore, after evaluation of his entire evidence and the material placed on record, this Court is of the considered opinion, atleast 10% of disability is to be taken into consideration so far as the other injuries as concerned.
Thus, in all, petitioner has suffered 40% disability of the whole body.
Therefore, compensation is required to be calculated by taking disability at 40%.
17 . During the course of the arguments, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that even in case of personal injury, the petitioner is entitled for loss of future prospects.

In support of his contention, he has relied upon the decisions of the Division Bench of this Court in MFA No.103807/2016 and connected matter and MFA No.202456/2018, wherein it is held that even in case of personal injury affecting the earning capacity, future prospects are required to be added.
18. Loss of future income:

In the light of contention raised, having regard to the fact that at the time of accident, petitioner was aged below 40 years, as held in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd Vs.
Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram1, 40% of the income is required to be added in order to calculate the loss of income due to the injury sustained.

sentences.text: Therefore, the notional income of the petitioner is required to be taken at Rs.9,100/- per month.

Since the disability is held to be 40% of the whole body, the compensation under the head loss of future income is Rs.9,100 x 12 x 17 x 40% = Rs.7,42,560/- as against Rs.2,44,800/- granted by the Tribunal.

19. Medical expenses:
Based on the medical bills, the Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.70,768/- and it requires no interference.
20. Pain and Suffering:

Having regard to the nature of injuries suffered which has resulted in permanent partial disability, this Court is of the considered opinion that petitioner is entitled to compensation in a sum of Rs.40,000/- under the head 'Pain and Sufferings' as against Rs.30,000/-
granted by the Tribunal.
(2018) 18 SCC 130 21. Loss of amenities:

Similarly, he is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.30,000/- under the head 'Loss of Amenities' as against Rs.10,000/- granted by the Tribunal.
22. Loss of income during laid up period:

At the rate of Rs.6,500/- per month for a period of three months, petitioner is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.19,500/- under the head 'Loss of income during laid up period' as against Rs.18,000/- granted by the Tribunal.
23. Attendant's charges, food and conveyance:
However, compensation granted in a sum of Rs.10,000/- under the head 'Attendant's charges, food and conveyance' is enhanced to Rs.15,000/- including nutritious food.
24. Thus, in all petitioner is entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.9,17,828/- as against Rs.3,84,000/- granted by the Tribunal as detailed below:

Respondent No.2 has taken up a specific contention that petitioner has also contributed towards the cause of accident on the ground that while moving behind the offending vehicle, he has not maintained sufficient distance.
He was also over speeding and as such, he himself has dashed against the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: The contributory negligence for the cause of accident as alleged and pleaded by respondent No.2 is with reference to him not maintaining proper distance between the offending vehicle and the motor cycle and also over speeding.

26. In fact, PW-1 has been cross examined on this aspect, wherein he has deposed that offending vehicle was moving in a high speed whereas he was proceeding behind it by maintaining a distance of 15 to 20 feet in a moderate speed.
He has alleged that accident was caused when suddenly the driver of the offending vehicle applied brake.

If petitioner was moving in a moderate speed by maintaining a distance of 15 to 20 feet, even where the driver of the offending vehicle applied brake suddenly without giving any indication, then also petitioner would have sufficient time to apply brake and stop his vehicle instead of going and dashing against the offending vehicle.
This very fact goes to show that he had failed to maintain proper distance between his motor cycle and the offending vehicle and also he was over speeding.
As a result of which, he was unable to control the vehicle.
Therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that petitioner has contributed towards the cause of the accident.

Despite,
respondent No.2 taking up such a specific defence and cross examining PW-1 on that aspect, the Tribunal has not given any findings on the same.

27. Having regard to the evidence placed on record, taking into consideration of the fact that petitioner has also contributed towards the cause of accident, this Court is of the considered opinion that the contributory negligence to be attributed to the petitioner is 20%.
Therefore, out of the total compensation, 20% is required to be deducted towards the contributory negligence of the petitioner.
Therefore, petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,34,263/- as against Rs.3,84,000/- granted by the Tribunal.
28. Of course petitioner is entitled for interest at the rate of interest at 6% p.a on the enhanced compensation and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (
a) Appeal is allowed in part.
(b) The compensation is enhanced to  Rs.7,34,263/- as against  Rs.3,84,000/- granted by the  Tribunal.
